problem.summary: 现有目标检测模型在追求高精度的同时，模型尺寸和计算成本高昂，难以部署在机器人、自动驾驶等资源受限的实时应用中。需要一种能在广泛资源约束下实现高精度和高效率的检测器。

motivation.summary: 模型效率在计算机视觉中日益重要。现有高效检测器通常牺牲精度，且大多只关注特定或小范围的资源需求。需要系统性地研究网络架构设计选择，提出关键优化以提高效率。

core_idea.summary: 提出两个关键优化：1) 加权双向特征金字塔网络（BiFPN），实现简单快速的多尺度特征融合；2) 复合缩放方法，统一缩放骨干网络、特征网络和分类/回归网络的分辨率、深度和宽度。结合EfficientNet骨干网络，开发出一系列高效检测器EfficientDet。

method.summary: 基于单阶段检测器范式，设计骨干网络（EfficientNet）、特征网络（BiFPN）和分类/回归预测网络。BiFPN通过引入可学习权重和双向跨尺度连接优化特征融合。复合缩放方法使用一个复合系数φ联合缩放所有维度。

experiments.summary: 在COCO 2017检测数据集上评估。EfficientDet-D7在test-dev上达到52.2 AP，参数52M，FLOPs 325B，比先前最佳检测器小4-9倍，FLOPs少13-42倍。在Pascal VOC 2012语义分割上也展示了优越性能。

claims.claim: BiFPN通过加权特征融合和双向连接，比FPN、PANet和NAS-FPN更有效。
复合缩放方法比单一维度缩放更能提高效率。
EfficientDet在广泛资源约束下实现了最先进的精度和效率。
EfficientDet在GPU和CPU上比先前检测器快4-11倍。
快速归一化融合在保持精度的同时比softmax融合快30%。

limitations.limitation: 复合缩放方法是启发式的，可能不是最优的。BiFPN的层数（重复次数）需要根据资源约束通过复合缩放确定。

nodes.title: 骨干网络
nodes.label: Backbone
nodes.summary: 使用EfficientNet作为骨干网络，提取多尺度特征。
nodes.description: EfficientNet系列网络，通过复合缩放平衡网络深度、宽度和分辨率，提供高效的特征提取。

nodes.title: 加权双向特征金字塔网络
nodes.label: BiFPN
nodes.summary: 提出BiFPN，通过可学习权重和双向跨尺度连接进行高效的多尺度特征融合。
nodes.description: BiFPN移除仅有一个输入边的节点，添加从原始输入到输出的跳跃连接，并重复应用双向跨尺度连接。使用快速归一化融合（Fast Normalized Fusion）加权融合不同分辨率的特征。

nodes.title: 分类/回归预测网络
nodes.label: Class/Box Network
nodes.summary: 共享特征的分类和边界框回归预测网络。
nodes.description: 分类和回归网络共享特征，其深度通过复合缩放方法确定。

nodes.title: 复合缩放方法
nodes.label: Compound Scaling
nodes.summary: 提出复合缩放方法，使用一个复合系数φ联合缩放骨干网络、BiFPN、分类/回归网络和输入分辨率。
nodes.description: 缩放规则：BiFPN宽度W_bifpn = 64 * (1.35^φ)，深度D_bifpn = 3 + φ；分类/回归网络深度D_box = D_class = 3 + floor(φ/3)；输入分辨率R_input = 512 + φ*128。

nodes.title: EfficientDet检测器
nodes.label: EfficientDet
nodes.summary: 结合EfficientNet骨干、BiFPN和复合缩放，开发出一系列高效检测器（D0-D7）。
nodes.description: 整体架构遵循单阶段检测器范式，使用EfficientNet骨干、BiFPN特征网络和共享的分类/回归预测头。

edges.label: 特征输入
edges.description: 骨干网络提取的多尺度特征输入到BiFPN进行融合。

edges.label: 融合特征输出
edges.description: BiFPN融合后的特征输出到分类/回归预测网络。

edges.label: 缩放骨干
edges.description: 复合缩放方法决定骨干网络的缩放（通过选择EfficientNet变体）。

edges.label: 缩放BiFPN
edges.description: 复合缩放方法决定BiFPN的宽度和深度（重复次数）。

edges.label: 缩放预测头
edges.description: 复合缩放方法决定分类/回归网络的深度。

deltas.after: 使用EfficientNet系列作为骨干网络。
deltas.why_it_matters: EfficientNet通过复合缩放平衡深度、宽度和分辨率，比ResNet具有更好的精度-效率权衡。

deltas.before: 使用FPN（自上而下的单向路径）进行多尺度特征融合。
deltas.after: 使用BiFPN（双向跨尺度连接和加权特征融合）。
deltas.why_it_matters: BiFPN通过双向信息流和可学习权重，更有效地融合不同分辨率的特征，显著提升精度并减少参数和计算量。

deltas.before: 通常通过单一维度（如增大骨干、增大输入图像）缩放检测器。
deltas.after: 提出复合缩放方法，使用一个复合系数φ联合缩放骨干、BiFPN、预测网络和输入分辨率。
deltas.why_it_matters: 联合缩放能更好地平衡不同架构维度，比单一维度缩放获得更好的效率。

deltas.before: 特征融合中，不同输入特征被平等对待（简单求和）。
deltas.after: 引入快速归一化融合（Fast Normalized Fusion），为每个输入特征分配可学习的权重。
deltas.why_it_matters: 不同分辨率的特征对输出的贡献不同，加权融合能学习其重要性，提升融合效果。快速归一化融合在保持精度的同时比softmax融合快30%。

formulas.name: 快速归一化融合

variables.name: O
variables.description: 融合后的输出特征

variables.name: I_i
variables.description: 第i个输入特征

variables.name: w_i
variables.description: 第i个输入特征的可学习权重（通过ReLU确保非负）

variables.name: \epsilon
variables.description: 小常数（0.0001），避免数值不稳定

formulas.intuition: 为每个输入特征分配一个可学习的权重，权重经过归一化（除以权重和加一个小常数）后用于加权求和。这比softmax融合更快，且能学习不同特征的重要性。

formulas.name: BiFPN中间特征计算（以第6层为例）

variables.name: P^{td}_{6}
variables.description: 第6层自上而下路径的中间特征

variables.name: P^{in}_{6}, P^{in}_{7}
variables.description: 骨干网络输出的第6层和第7层输入特征

variables.name: w_1, w_2
variables.description: 可学习权重

variables.name: \text{Resize}
variables.description: 上采样或下采样操作以匹配分辨率

variables.name: \text{Conv}
variables.description: 卷积操作（通常为深度可分离卷积）

formulas.intuition: BiFPN自上而下路径中，对同一层的输入特征和来自更高层的特征进行加权融合，然后通过卷积处理。

formulas.name: BiFPN输出特征计算（以第6层为例）
formulas.latex: P^{out}_{6} = \text{Conv}\left( \frac{w'_1 \cdot P^{in}_{6} + w'_2 \cdot P^{td}_{6} + w'_3 \cdot \text{Resize}(P^{out}_{5})}{w'_1 + w'_2 + w'_3 + \epsilon} \right)

variables.name: P^{out}_{6}
variables.description: 第6层自下而上路径的输出特征

variables.name: P^{in}_{6}
variables.description: 骨干网络输出的第6层输入特征

variables.name: P^{td}_{6}
variables.description: 自上而下路径的中间特征

variables.name: P^{out}_{5}
variables.description: 第5层自下而上路径的输出特征

variables.name: w'_1, w'_2, w'_3
variables.description: 可学习权重

formulas.intuition: BiFPN自下而上路径中，融合原始输入特征、自上而下路径的中间特征以及来自更低层的输出特征，实现双向信息流。

formulas.name: 复合缩放 - BiFPN宽度

variables.name: W_{bifpn}
variables.description: BiFPN的通道宽度

variables.name: \phi
variables.description: 复合系数，控制所有缩放维度

formulas.intuition: BiFPN的通道宽度随复合系数φ指数增长。

formulas.name: 复合缩放 - BiFPN深度

variables.name: D_{bifpn}
variables.description: BiFPN的深度（重复次数）

variables.name: \phi
variables.description: 复合系数

formulas.intuition: BiFPN的深度（重复应用的次数）随φ线性增加。

formulas.name: 复合缩放 - 分类/回归网络深度

variables.name: D_{box}, D_{class}
variables.description: 边界框回归和分类网络的深度

variables.name: \phi
variables.description: 复合系数

formulas.intuition: 分类和回归网络的深度增长较慢，每增加3个φ单位深度增加1。

formulas.name: 复合缩放 - 输入分辨率

variables.name: R_{input}
variables.description: 输入图像的分辨率（假设为正方形）

variables.name: \phi
variables.description: 复合系数

formulas.intuition: 输入分辨率随φ线性增加，从512开始，每增加1个φ，分辨率增加128像素。

glossary.BiFPN: 加权双向特征金字塔网络（Weighted Bi-directional Feature Pyramid Network），一种用于多尺度特征融合的网络结构，具有双向跨尺度连接和可学习的特征融合权重。
glossary.复合缩放: Compound Scaling，使用一个复合系数φ联合缩放检测器的所有维度（骨干网络、特征网络、预测网络、输入分辨率）。
glossary.快速归一化融合: Fast Normalized Fusion，BiFPN中使用的特征融合方法，通过归一化的可学习权重对输入特征进行加权求和，比softmax融合更快。
glossary.EfficientNet: 一系列通过复合缩放设计的高效卷积神经网络，用作EfficientDet的骨干网络。
glossary.单阶段检测器: One-Stage Detector，没有显式区域提议步骤的目标检测器，直接从图像预测边界框和类别。
glossary.FLOPs: 浮点运算数（Floating Point Operations），衡量模型计算复杂度的指标。
glossary.深度可分离卷积: Depthwise Separable Convolution，一种高效的卷积操作，将标准卷积分解为深度卷积和逐点卷积，减少参数和计算量。
glossary.复合系数: Compound Coefficient (φ)，控制EfficientDet模型缩放的单一参数，φ越大，模型越大。

steps.description: 2. 实现EfficientNet骨干网络（或使用现有实现）。
3. 实现BiFPN特征网络，包括快速归一化融合和双向跨尺度连接。
4. 实现共享的分类/回归预测网络。
5. 实现复合缩放方法，根据φ生成不同配置（D0-D7）。
6. 使用SGD优化器（动量0.9，权重衰减4e-5）训练，学习率预热后余弦退火。
7. 训练时使用水平翻转和尺度抖动（0.1x-2.0x）数据增强。
9. 在COCO val和test-dev上评估AP，在Pascal VOC上评估mIOU。

metadata.title: EfficientDet: Scalable and Efficient Object Detection
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Detection / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: Model efficiency has become increasingly important in computer vision. In this paper, we systematically study neural network architecture design choices for object detection and propose several key optimizations to improve efficiency. First, we propose a weighted bi-directional feature pyramid network (BiFPN), which allows easy and fast multi-scale feature fusion; Second, we propose a compound scaling method that uniformly scales the resolution, depth, and width for all backbone, feature network, and box/class prediction networks at the same time. Based on these optimizations and EfficientNet backbones, we have developed a new family of object detectors, called EfficientDet, which consistently achieve much better efficiency than prior art across a wide spectrum of resource constraints. In particular, with single-model and single-scale, our EfficientDetD7 achieves state-of-the-art 52.2 AP on COCO test-dev with 52M parameters and 325B FLOPs, being 4x – 9x smaller and using 13x – 42x fewer FLOPs than previous detector.

Moreover, most previous works only focus on a speciﬁc or a small range of resource requirements, but the variety of real-world applications, from mobile devices to datacenters, often demand different resource constraints. A natural question is: Is it possible to build a scal- able detection architecture with both higher accuracy and better efﬁciency across a wide spectrum of resource con- straints (e.g., from 3B to 300B FLOPs)? While fusing dif- ferent input features, most previous works simply sum them up without distinction; however, since these different input features are at different resolutions, we observe they usu- ally contribute to the fused output feature unequally. To address this issue, we propose a simple yet highly effective weighted bi-directional feature pyramid network (BiFPN), which introduces learnable weights to learn the importance of different input features, while repeatedly applying top- down and bottom-up multi-scale feature fusion. Challenge 2: model scaling – While previous works mainly rely on bigger backbone networks [24, 35, 34, 10] or
larger input image sizes [13, 45] for higher accuracy, we ob-

serve that scaling up feature network and box/class predic- tion network is also critical when taking into account both accuracy and efﬁciency. Inspired by recent works [39], we propose a compound scaling method for object detectors, which jointly scales up the resolution/depth/width for all backbone, feature network, box/class prediction network. Finally, we also observe that the recently introduced Efﬁ- cientNets [39] achieve better efﬁciency than previous com- monly used backbones. Combining EfﬁcientNet backbones with our propose BiFPN and compound scaling, we have developed a new family of object detectors, named Efﬁ- cientDet, which consistently achieve better accuracy with much fewer parameters and FLOPs than previous object detectors. Related Work One-Stage Detectors: Existing object detectors are mostly categorized by whether they have a region-of- interest proposal step (two-stage [11, 35, 5, 13]) or not (one- stage [36, 27, 33, 24]). While two-stage detectors tend to be more ﬂexible and more accurate, one-stage detectors are of- ten considered to be simpler and more efﬁcient by leverag- ing predeﬁned anchors [17]. Recently, one-stage detectors have attracted substantial attention due to their efﬁciency and simplicity [21, 42, 44]. In this paper, we mainly follow the one-stage detector design, and we show it is possible to achieve both better efﬁciency and higher accuracy with optimized network architectures. Multi-Scale Feature Representations: One of the main difﬁculties in object detection is to effectively represent and process multi-scale features. Earlier detectors often directly perform predictions based on the pyramidal feature hierar- chy extracted from back...

Cross-Scale Connections Conventional top-down FPN is inherently limited by the one-way information ﬂow. To address this issue, PANet [26] adds an extra bottom-up path aggregation network, as shown in Figure 2(b). Cross-scale connections are further studied in [20, 18, 42]. Recently, NAS-FPN [10] employs neural architecture search to search for better cross-scale
feature network topology, but it requires thousands of GPU

hours during search and the found network is irregular and difﬁcult to interpret or modify, as shown in Figure 2(c). By studying the performance and efﬁciency of these three networks (Table 5), we observe that PANet achieves better accuracy than FPN and NAS-FPN, but with the cost of more parameters and computations. To improve model efﬁciency, this paper proposes several optimizations for cross-scale connections: First, we remove those nodes that only have one input edge. Our intuition is simple: if a node has only one input edge with no feature fusion, then it will have less contribution to feature network that aims at fusing different features. This leads to a simpliﬁed bi- directional network; Second, we add an extra edge from the original input to output node if they are at the same level, in order to fuse more features without adding much cost; Third, unlike PANet [26] that only has one top-down and one bottom-up path, we treat each bidirectional (top-down & bottom-up) path as on...
ture fusion. Section 4.2 will discuss how to determine the

number of layers for different resource constraints using a compound scaling method. With these optimizations, we name the new feature network as bidirectional feature pyra- mid network (BiFPN), as shown in Figure 2 and 3. 3.3. Weighted Feature Fusion When fusing features with different resolutions, a com- mon way is to ﬁrst resize them to the same resolution and then sum them up. Pyramid attention network [22] intro- duces global self-attention upsampling to recover pixel lo- calization, which is further studied in [10]. All previous methods treat all input features equally without distinction. However, we observe that since different input features are at different resolutions, they usually contribute to the output feature unequally. To address this issue, we propose to add an additional weight for each input, and let the network to learn the importance of each input feature. Aiming at optimizing both accuracy and efﬁciency, we

would like to develop a family of models that can meet a wide spectrum of resource constraints. A key challenge here is how to scale up a baseline EfﬁcientDet model. Previous works mostly scale up a baseline detector by employing bigger backbone networks ( e.g., ResNeXt [41]

Conclusion In this paper, we systematically study network architec- ture design choices for efﬁcient object detection, and pro- pose a weighted bidirectional feature network and a cus- tomized compound scaling method, in order to improve ac- curacy and efﬁciency. Based on these optimizations, we de- velop a new family of detectors, named EfﬁcientDet, which consistently achieve better accuracy and efﬁciency than the prior art across a wide spectrum of resource constraints. In particular, our scaled EfﬁcientDet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with much fewer parameters and FLOPs than pre- vious object detection and semantic segmentation models. Hyperparameters Neural network architecture and training hyperparamters are both crucial for object detection. Here we ablate two important hyperparamters: training epochs and multi-scale jittering, using RetinaNet-R50 and our EfﬁcientDet-D1. All other hyperparameters are kept the same as section 5. 3...
Figure 7: Accuracy vs. Training Epochs.

Training Epochs: Many previous work only use a small number of epochs: for example, Detectron2 [1] trains each model with 12 epochs (1x schedule) in default, and at most 110 epochs (9x scahedule). Recent work [12] shows train- ing longer is not helpful if using pretrained backbone net- works; however, we observe training longer can signiﬁ- ciantly improve accuracy in our settings. Figure 7 shows the performance comparison for different training epochs. We obseve: (1) both models beneﬁt from longer training until reaching 300 epochs; (2) longer training is particularly important for EfﬁcientDet, perhaps due to its small model size; (3) compared to the default 37 AP [24], our reproduced RetinaNet achieves higher accuracy (+2AP) using our train- ing settings. In this paper, we mainly use 300 epochs for the good trade-off between accuracy and training time. Scale Jittering: A common training-time augmentation is to ﬁrst resize images and then crop them into ﬁxed size, known as scale jitte...

1.2. Image Resolutions In addition to our compound scaling that progres- sively increases image sizes, we are also interested in the accuracy-latency trade-offs with ﬁxed image resolutions.
Figure 9 compares EfﬁcientDet-D1 to D6 with ﬁxed and

scaled resolutions. Surprisingly, their accuracy-latency trade-offs are very similar even though they have very different preferences: under similar accuracy constraints, models with ﬁxed resolutions require much more param- eters, but less activations and peak memory usage, than those with scaled resolutions.
